dish:Garotes (eriçó de mar / sea urchin).name: Garotes (eriçó de mar / sea urchin)
dish:Garotes (eriçó de mar / sea urchin).label: SEASON (winter, ~Dec–Mar) / FEAST-DAY (Garoinada campaign)
dish:Garotes (eriçó de mar / sea urchin).hook: The cold-water rock harvest you eat raw, with a spoon, December to March.
dish:Garotes (eriçó de mar / sea urchin).text: The cold-water rock harvest you eat raw, with a spoon, December to March. €€–€€€ (market price, varies by catch) Lunch The violet-spined urchin (Paracentrotus lividus) clamps to the schist below the Cap de Creus cliffs; in the Alt Empordà it is the garota (garoïna further south). TECHNIQUE: split the shell across the mouth-side with scissors, rinse out the dark viscera and lift the five orange gonad 'tongues' — eaten raw on bread, or folded into scrambled eggs as ous amb garotes. The season runs roughly December–March, when the tramuntana calms the sea and the roe is fullest. Eat them at Cadaqués seafood tables in winter; the coast's set-piece is La Garoinada (Palafrugell/Llafranc/Calella de Palafrugell, 16 Jan–29 Mar 2026).

dish:Anxoves de l'Escala.name: Anxoves de l'Escala
dish:Anxoves de l'Escala.label: AT SOURCE (L'Escala salters; on Cadaqués tables)
dish:Anxoves de l'Escala.hook: Salt-cured anchovy from a 2,500-year-old trade, hand-filleted by women in L'Escala.
chips: €€ (a few euros per tin/plate; premium for hand-filleted)
dish:Anxoves de l'Escala.text: Salt-cured anchovy from a 2,500-year-old trade, hand-filleted by women in L'Escala. €€ (a few euros per tin/plate; premium for hand-filleted) Aperitiu / lunch Boquerons caught off the Costa Brava, then packed in salt for months and filleted by hand. The craft traces to fish-salting at Empúries (Greeks, 6th–5th c. BC); the salt warehouse Alfolí de la Sal was finished 1697. Houses Solés (1888) and Callol i Serrats (1847) still cure them; the product carries the 'Anxoves de l'Escala' quality mark. TECHNIQUE: desalt the filets briefly, dress with Empordà oil — never cook them. Eat plain on toast, or at Compartir (Cadaqués) where they pair the anchovy with almond cream.

dish:Suquet de peix.name: Suquet de peix
dish:Suquet de peix.label: AT SOURCE (Cadaqués/Costa Brava restaurants)
dish:Suquet de peix.hook: The fishermen's stew: rock fish and potato, thickened with an almond-saffron picada.
dish:Suquet de peix.text: The fishermen's stew: rock fish and potato, thickened with an almond-saffron picada. €€€ Lunch / dinner Built on the day's peix de roca (scorpionfish, rascasse, reef fish) and potatoes. TECHNIQUE: start a sofregit of slow-cooked onion and tomato, add fish and potato with a little water/fish stock, then finish in the last minutes with a picada of toasted almonds, garlic, fried bread, parsley and saffron pounded in the mortar — the picada both thickens and seasons; some cooks add a spoon of allioli at the end. Both the Empordà and Tarragona claim its origin. Order it at Cadaqués seafood houses (e.g. Compartir, Carrer del Sitjar 5).

dish:Arròs negre de l'Empordà.name: Arròs negre de l'Empordà
dish:Arròs negre de l'Empordà.label: AT SOURCE (Empordà restaurants)
dish:Arròs negre de l'Empordà.hook: Black rice darkened by cuttlefish ink and an onion sofregit cooked almost to burning.
dish:Arròs negre de l'Empordà.text: Black rice darkened by cuttlefish ink and an onion sofregit cooked almost to burning. €€–€€€ Lunch The Empordà's signature rice. TECHNIQUE: the colour comes from cuttlefish (sèpia) ink AND a very long, dark onion sofregit — traditionally in a ceramic cassola, sometimes with pork lard — finished with a picada; served with allioli on the side. The Baix Empordà version is the textbook one, and the Garoinada offers an 'arròs negre amb sèpia' garnished with urchin roe. Widely cooked across Cadaqués and the Empordà.

dish:Peix de roca a la planxa / al forn.name: Peix de roca a la planxa / al forn
dish:Peix de roca a la planxa / al forn.label: AT SOURCE (Cadaqués; catch-dependent)
dish:Peix de roca a la planxa / al forn.hook: Whatever the schist coast gives up that morning, simply grilled.
dish:Peix de roca a la planxa / al forn.text: Whatever the schist coast gives up that morning, simply grilled. €€€ (priced by weight) Lunch / dinner Scorpionfish, sea bream, John Dory and the small rock fish that live in the Cap de Creus slate. TECHNIQUE: griddled or baked whole, dressed only with Empordà oil, garlic and parsley, so the firmness and iodine of line-caught fish carry the plate. At Casa Anita (Carrer Miquel Roset 16, Cadaqués) there is no printed menu — the waiters recite the day's catch; the room has fed Dalí among others.

dish:Es niu (Palafrugell).name: Es niu (Palafrugell)
dish:Es niu (Palafrugell).label: FEAST-DAY / SEASON (winter 'Es Niu' campaign, Palafrugell)
dish:Es niu (Palafrugell).hook: A five-hour winter stew of cod tripe, stockfish and game — the cork country's marathon dish.
dish:Es niu (Palafrugell).text: A five-hour winter stew of cod tripe, stockfish and game — the cork country's marathon dish. €€€ Lunch A Baix Empordà / Palafrugell dish (the cork-workers' country, not strictly Cadaqués) but part of the same Costa Brava winter table. TECHNIQUE: cod tripe (durícies), stockfish (peixopalo/bacallà), hard egg and potato over a long sofregit, slow-cooked ~5 hours to a honeyed, gelatinous body; cuttlefish and game birds were later additions. Originally a Lenten, meatless fishermen's dish from the 19th century. Look for it during Palafrugell's 'Es Niu' winter campaign.

dish:Compartir's sharing table (elBulli.name: Compartir's sharing table (elBulli lineage)
dish:Compartir's sharing table (elBulli.label: AT SOURCE (book ahead)
dish:Compartir's sharing table (elBulli.hook: The Disfrutar trio's Cadaqués room — elBulli technique on the village's produce.
dish:Compartir's sharing table (elBulli.text: The Disfrutar trio's Cadaqués room — elBulli technique on the village's produce. €€€€ (~€80–87 tasting) Dinner Opened April 2012 by Mateu Casañas, Oriol Castro and Eduard Xatruch, former head chefs of elBulli (Cala Montjoi, Roses, ~30 min up the coast) for 15 years; they later opened three-Michelin-star Disfrutar in Barcelona (Dec 2014). TECHNIQUE: shared plates that rework local catch with elBulli method — anchovy with almond cream, fish en papillote, modernised suquet. Michelin lists it under 'Good cooking' (the Plate, no star); tasting menus run roughly €80–87. Carrer del Sitjar 5, Cadaqués.

calas:Platja de Portlligat.name: Platja de Portlligat
calas:Platja de Portlligat.text: On foot 15-20 min north over the hill from Cadaques centre, or 5 min by car with parking at the bay 170 m of grey shingle and cobble (no sand), facing east across the still bay that fronts Dali's house at Portlligat; sheltered water, full of moored fishing boats Open in Google Maps →

calas:Platja Gran de Cadaques.name: Platja Gran de Cadaques
calas:Platja Gran de Cadaques.text: In the centre, straight off the seafront promenade by the Dali statue The 200 m x 20 m town beach, coarse sand over pebbles, easy entry and the busiest stretch in summer; faces the open bay so the tramuntana pushes chop straight in Open in Google Maps →

calas:Platja de Sa Conca.name: Platja de Sa Conca
calas:Platja de Sa Conca.text: On foot 15-20 min south along the shore promenade from the centre, or by car with a small lot above 100 m half-moon of coarse sand and pebbles, rocky seabed that drops off quickly; long nudist tradition and home of the Cadaques International Music Festival since 1970 Open in Google Maps →

calas:Es Sortell.name: Es Sortell
calas:Es Sortell.text: On foot about 1 km south past Sa Conca, parking roughly 300 m above Small 50 m grey gravel-and-rock cove with a stone footbridge out to the Sortell islet and pines wedged in the schist; shallow, calm, some of the best views back at the white village Open in Google Maps →

calas:S'Alqueria Gran.name: S'Alqueria Gran
calas:S'Alqueria Gran.text: By car about 2 km on the Cap de Creus lighthouse road then a short walk down; no dedicated parking About 60 m of pebbles and coarse sand in the Raco des Mor bay, no services, clear water and a nudist habit; set among dense scrub and rock Open in Google Maps →

calas:Cala Nans (Far de Cala Nans).name: Cala Nans (Far de Cala Nans)
calas:Cala Nans (Far de Cala Nans).text: Coastal path on foot from the centre, 3.6 km / about 1h15 each way from trail marker AE-141; rock-entry swimming, no beach A rocky inlet at the far eastern end of the bay below the 1874 lighthouse (light 36 m above the sea, range 8 nautical miles); schist ledges to swim off, fully exposed to the tramuntana Open in Google Maps →

calas:Cala Culip.name: Cala Culip
calas:Cala Culip.text: By car to the Cap de Creus lighthouse (8 km / 20 min) then 10 min down the slope, or on foot via the Cami de Ronda in about 1h30 Tiny 15 m shingle-and-rock cove at the foot of the lighthouse, sheltered and clear; sponges, starfish and moray on the snorkel, and seabed of ancient wrecks (Culip IV, c. 70-80 AD) Open in Google Maps →

calas:Cala Jugadora.name: Cala Jugadora
calas:Cala Jugadora.text: By car to the Cap de Creus lighthouse then 10 min down a slope path, 7 km north of Cadaques A 15 m pocket of coarse sand and gravel right under the Cap de Creus lighthouse, sheltered from the tramuntana; seabed of rock, sand tongues and Posidonia for snorkelling Open in Google Maps →

walks:Cami de Ronda: Platja de Cadaques.name: Cami de Ronda: Platja de Cadaques to Far de Cala Nans
walks:Cami de Ronda: Platja de Cadaques.hook: The bay's eastern lip, white houses then bare schist, ending at an 1874 lighthouse.
chips: 3.6 km one way, about 1h15 each way (around 8 km / 2h50 return)
Late afternoon for the light on the white village; avoid days of hard tramuntana
walks:Cami de Ronda: Platja de Cadaques.text: The bay's eastern lip, white houses then bare schist, ending at an 1874 lighthouse. 3.6 km one way, about 1h15 each way (around 8 km / 2h50 return) Late afternoon for the light on the white village; avoid days of hard tramuntana From trail marker AE-141 at the south end of the village the path threads past Punta des Baluard, the Port de l'Alguer and Punta d'en Pampa before the houses give out and the route runs into open Cap de Creus rock as far as the Cala Nans light, inaugurated 1 September 1874, its lamp 36 m above the sea with a range of 8 nautical miles. Rated easy; rock-entry swimming below the far, no beach. Full exposure to the tramuntana on the headland. Open in Google Maps →

walks:Cami Antic: Portlligat to the Far.name: Cami Antic: Portlligat to the Far de Cap de Creus
walks:Cami Antic: Portlligat to the Far.hook: The old path cove-to-cove to the easternmost lighthouse on the Iberian peninsula.
chips: 5.54 km one way / about 2h20 (roughly 14.8 km / 4h return from Cadaques)
Morning start to reach the cape before the midday crowds; clear days for the Pyrenees-to-sea panorama
walks:Cami Antic: Portlligat to the Far.text: The old path cove-to-cove to the easternmost lighthouse on the Iberian peninsula. 5.54 km one way / about 2h20 (roughly 14.8 km / 4h return from Cadaques) Morning start to reach the cape before the midday crowds; clear days for the Pyrenees-to-sea panorama Start at the AE-252 junction on the Portlligat beach; the route crosses the road to Cala Es Jonquet and Platja de Sant Lluis, reaches Guillola beach and the Cami Antic turnoff, then climbs through abandoned vineyard and olive terraces with the lighthouse always on the skyline. Yellow paint marks the way. The Far del Cap de Creus light entered service the night of 29 July 1853, the second oldest in Catalonia, marking the easternmost point of mainland Spain. Open in Google Maps →

walks:Cap de Creus lighthouse + Cala Cul.name: Cap de Creus lighthouse + Cala Culip loop
walks:Cap de Creus lighthouse + Cala Cul.hook: Park at the cape, drop to a sheltered cove over Roman wrecks, climb back to the light.
chips: About 4 km loop, 1.5-2 h with a swim
Late morning when the sun is on the cove water; avoid rough-sea days
walks:Cap de Creus lighthouse + Cala Cul.text: Park at the cape, drop to a sheltered cove over Roman wrecks, climb back to the light. About 4 km loop, 1.5-2 h with a swim Late morning when the sun is on the cove water; avoid rough-sea days From the lighthouse car park a 10-minute slope path drops to Cala Culip, a 15 m shingle cove sheltered from the tramuntana with a snorkel-able seabed holding ancient wrecks (Culip IV, c. 70-80 AD). The short Paratge de Tudela-Cala Culip circuit runs about 4 km. Leave the lighthouse path and step a few dozen metres right to look down on the cove; Cala Jugadora and Cala Fredosa sit just south. Open in Google Maps →

walks:Cadaques to the Ermita de Sant Seb.name: Cadaques to the Ermita de Sant Sebastia (Peni viewpoint)
walks:Cadaques to the Ermita de Sant Seb.hook: A thyme-and-rosemary climb to the balcony over the whole bay.
chips: Early morning before the heat for the climb; clear days for the Roses-bay and Pyrenees views
walks:Cadaques to the Ermita de Sant Seb.text: A thyme-and-rosemary climb to the balcony over the whole bay. About 8 km, +350 m, roughly 2h30 Early morning before the heat for the climb; clear days for the Roses-bay and Pyrenees views From the village the path climbs the eastern flank of Puig Peni through scrub of thyme, rosemary and rockrose to the 18th-century hermitage of Sant Sebastia de Peni, sited at about 385 m and held in private hands since 1890 (its romeria falls every 20 January). The bay of Cadaques, the coves below and Cala Nans with its lighthouse open up underfoot. The Peni summit proper (606 m) carries the EVA-4 military radar and is closed to the public, so this hermitage is the viewpoint to aim for. Open in Google Maps →

walks:GR-92 Cami de Ronda stretch: Cadaq.name: GR-92 Cami de Ronda stretch: Cadaques to El Port de la Selva
walks:GR-92 Cami de Ronda stretch: Cadaq.hook: The long-distance coast path over the spine of the peninsula to the next bay.
chips: About 12 km, roughly 3 h one way to El Port de la Selva
Cooler months or an early start; carry water, there is no shade or service on the ridge
walks:GR-92 Cami de Ronda stretch: Cadaq.text: The long-distance coast path over the spine of the peninsula to the next bay. About 12 km, roughly 3 h one way to El Port de la Selva Cooler months or an early start; carry water, there is no shade or service on the ridge The GR-92 runs the length of the Catalan coast from Portbou to Ulldecona; the Cadaques leg heads inland and uphill on stony paths across the Cap de Creus reserve to El Port de la Selva, with the Sant Pere de Rodes monastery and Sant Salvador de Verdera in reach on the longer circuit. A demanding stage of bare schist, wind-bent vegetation and big sea views rather than a stroll. Open in Google Maps →

walks:The olive-terrace path (Cami Antic.name: The olive-terrace path (Cami Antic through the abandoned vinyes)
walks:The olive-terrace path (Cami Antic.hook: Dry-stone terraces of dead vineyards, now sage, thyme and olive, framing the lighthouse.
chips: About 45 min of the path section to the lighthouse; part of the 14.8 km / 4 h Cami Antic return
Spring for flowering rockrose and broom on the terraces; soft light late afternoon
walks:The olive-terrace path (Cami Antic.text: Dry-stone terraces of dead vineyards, now sage, thyme and olive, framing the lighthouse. About 45 min of the path section to the lighthouse; part of the 14.8 km / 4 h Cami Antic return Spring for flowering rockrose and broom on the terraces; soft light late afternoon The middle section of the Cami Antic, once past Guillola beach, climbs through orchards of sage, thyme and olive trees on the abandoned dry-stone vineyard terraces that once carried the Garnatxa and Carinyena vines of this coast, the Cap de Creus lighthouse profile held in the distance the whole way. The slate walls, built by hand against the slope, are the human grain of the peninsula's schist. Open in Google Maps →

walks:Far de Cala Nans short out-and-bac.name: Far de Cala Nans short out-and-back
walks:Far de Cala Nans short out-and-bac.hook: The compact half-day version: the bay's edge to the white tower and back.
chips: Golden hour for the lighthouse and the village across the water
walks:Far de Cala Nans short out-and-bac.text: The compact half-day version: the bay's edge to the white tower and back. About 7-8 km return, 2h30-2h50 Golden hour for the lighthouse and the village across the water Roughly 3 km of well-marked coast path from the centre to the Cala Nans light and straight back, the easiest way to taste the Cami de Ronda without committing to the full Cap de Creus crossing. Schist ledges below the far take rock-entry swims on a calm day; on a tramuntana day the spray comes over the path itself. Open in Google Maps →

coffee-gardens:Bar Marítim.name: Bar Marítim
coffee-gardens:Bar Marítim.label: WATERFRONT
coffee-gardens:Bar Marítim.text: Passeig Marítim (waterfront) Breakfast nearly in the water, facing the cone-shaped Cucurucú rock that is the village's emblem — open on the Passeig since 1935 (90 years in 2025), a Dalí haunt. Open in Google Maps →

coffee-gardens:Es Baluard.name: Es Baluard
coffee-gardens:Es Baluard.label: SEAFRONT
coffee-gardens:Es Baluard.text: Old town wall / seafront Coffee on a terrace built into the old town wall, wide-open over the harbour — family-run since 1967, right on the sea front. Open in Google Maps →

coffee-gardens:L'Hostal.name: L'Hostal
coffee-gardens:L'Hostal.label: DALÍ'S BAR
coffee-gardens:L'Hostal.text: Plaça Passeig (town centre) Sit where Dalí drank — the one bar he frequented, whose logo he drew and signed for free; now a daytime tapas-and-drinks room on the central plaça that keeps the old nighthawk décor. Open in Google Maps →

coffee-gardens:Es Cucurucú viewpoint (mi.name: Es Cucurucú viewpoint (mirador)
coffee-gardens:Es Cucurucú viewpoint (mi.label: MIRADOR
coffee-gardens:Es Cucurucú viewpoint (mi.text: Northern end of the bay The headland by the cone rock that gives the village its symbol — a stand-and-look point over the whole bay rather than a café, best paired with a takeaway coffee from the Passeig (coords approximate, unverified). Open in Google Maps →

culture:Casa-Museu Salvador Dalí — Portl.name: Casa-Museu Salvador Dalí — Portlligat
culture:Casa-Museu Salvador Dalí — Portl.hook: The labyrinthine fisherman's-shack house where Dalí lived 1930–1982, entered in groups of a handful every ten minutes.
culture:Casa-Museu Salvador Dalí — Portl.text: The labyrinthine fisherman's-shack house where Dalí lived 1930–1982, entered in groups of a handful every ten minutes. Dalí bought a one-room hut from the fisherman Lídia Noguer in 1930 and spent fifty years annexing the cottages around it into a warren of seven levels that climb the Portlligat hillside — the egg-topped tower, the oval Gala room, the studio with its sunken easel pit, and the lip-shaped sofa. The Fundació Gala-Salvador Dalí runs it as timed-entry only: groups enter every 10 minutes, self-guided with staff stationed inside, and advance booking is always required. The olive grove and pool with the Michelin-man Pirelli figure are visible from the cheaper grounds ticket. It is not wheelchair-accessible — the house is all narrow stairs and split levels. Closed 7 January to 11 February each year. Book timed tickets in advance at salvador-dali.org; arrive 30 min before your slot or the ticket is voided (no refunds). T. +34 972 677 500 / reserves@fundaciodali.org · €15 online / €17 at the door full; €12 / €14 reduced (students, over-65s); olive-grove-only €8 / €6; free ages 0–8. Verified on the Fundació site, 2025 rates. · Jun 15–Sep 13 daily 09:30–20:00; most of the rest of the year Tue–Sun 10:30–18:00; closed Jan 7–Feb 11. · Open in Google Maps →

culture:Església de Santa Maria — the fi.name: Església de Santa Maria — the fishermen's altarpiece
culture:Església de Santa Maria — the fi.hook: A 23-metre baroque retaule of gilded wood, paid for by the fishermen's brotherhood, carved 1723–1729 and not fully gilded until 1788.
culture:Església de Santa Maria — the fi.text: A 23-metre baroque retaule of gilded wood, paid for by the fishermen's brotherhood, carved 1723–1729 and not fully gilded until 1788. The whitewashed church crowns the old town; climb the stepped, schist-cobbled lanes (the local stone is slate/schist, set on edge) to reach it. Inside, the main altarpiece by the sculptors Pau Costa and Joan Torras rises 23 metres by 12 — a gilded baroque façade in five tiers, from a predella of Passion scenes up through the Marian central body to the attic, with the four Evangelists and the Coronation of the Virgin. The carving was done 1723–1729; the gold leaf was only finished in 1788, financed across decades by the town's fishermen, whose brotherhood paid for the work. Summer church concerts of the Festival de Música use the nave for its acoustics. Visiting hours are not officially published online — verify locally. Free entry outside service hours; the church doubles as a festival concert venue in summer (ticketed for those events). · Free to visit; festival concerts ticketed separately. · Generally open daytime; verify locally — hours not officially published online. · Open in Google Maps →

culture:Far de Cap de Creus — the lighth.name: Far de Cap de Creus — the lighthouse at Iberia's edge
culture:Far de Cap de Creus — the lighth.hook: The easternmost point of mainland Spain, lit since 29 July 1853, on a wind-scoured headland of folded schist.
culture:Far de Cap de Creus — the lighth.text: The easternmost point of mainland Spain, lit since 29 July 1853, on a wind-scoured headland of folded schist. Drive or walk the 8 km of switchbacks east out of Cadaqués to the cape, where the lighthouse — operational since 29 July 1853 — stands above coves like Cala Fredosa and Cala Jugadora. This is the tramuntana's anvil: the north wind has twisted the schist and slate into the contorted shapes Dalí mined for his melted forms. The headland sits inside the Parc Natural de Cap de Creus, Catalonia's first marine-and-land natural park. A restaurant occupies the old keeper's building beside the tower; the views run from the Pyrenees to the open Mediterranean. Headland/exterior hours and any interior-museum fee are seasonal and not officially published — confirm before going. Free to reach the headland and lighthouse exterior; restaurant beside the tower for food/drink. Park at the cape (fills fast in summer). · Free (headland/exterior). · Headland open access; lighthouse interior museum opens seasonally (summer). · Open in Google Maps →

culture:Espai Cap de Creus — reading the.name: Espai Cap de Creus — reading the rock
culture:Espai Cap de Creus — reading the.hook: The natural-park interpretation centre at the cape that decodes the geology Dalí turned into Surrealism.
culture:Espai Cap de Creus — reading the.text: The natural-park interpretation centre at the cape that decodes the geology Dalí turned into Surrealism. Set in the converted buildings around the lighthouse, Espai Cap de Creus is the scientific visitor centre for the Parc Natural — it lays out the geological evolution of the peninsula (the folded schists, pegmatite veins and wind-eroded forms) alongside the flora and fauna of the headland. It is the place to understand why this coast looks the way it does before you walk the GR-11 trails out to the cape's tip. Opening is seasonal (mainly summer); confirm on the Parc Natural / Empordà Turisme listing before going. Visit alongside the lighthouse at the cape; opening is seasonal, check the Parc Natural / Empordà Turisme listing before going. · Check on site; small/free interpretation centre. · Seasonal (mainly summer); confirm before visiting. · Open in Google Maps →

culture:Museu de Cadaqués — the town's o.name: Museu de Cadaqués — the town's own gallery
culture:Museu de Cadaqués — the town's o.hook: A small museum in the centre running rotating shows on the artists who painted this bay — Dalí among them.
culture:Museu de Cadaqués — the town's o.text: A small museum in the centre running rotating shows on the artists who painted this bay — Dalí among them. Unlike the house at Portlligat, the Museu de Cadaqués sits in the heart of the old town and mounts temporary exhibitions tied to the village: painters and themes connected to Cadaqués and its light, with recurring shows on Salvador Dalí and on the Pitxot family, the local clan of artists and musicians who first drew Dalí into the colony. Compact, climate-controlled, a good hour out of the tramuntana. Hours below are from a tourism aggregator — verify against the museum before relying on them. (Check current opening hours before going.) Walk-in; centrally located in the old town. Check current exhibition before going. · Modest admission (confirm on site). · Closed Tuesdays; roughly Mon and Wed–Sat 10:30–17:30, Sun 10:30–14:00 (verify seasonally). · Open in Google Maps →

culture:The artist colony — why everyone.name: The artist colony — why everyone came
culture:The artist colony — why everyone.hook: Picasso painted here in 1910; by the 1920s–30s Cadaqués pulled in Duchamp, Lorca, Buñuel, Magritte and Éluard.
culture:The artist colony — why everyone.text: Picasso painted here in 1910; by the 1920s–30s Cadaqués pulled in Duchamp, Lorca, Buñuel, Magritte and Éluard. Cadaqués was a hard-to-reach fishing village — no easy road until the 20th century — which is exactly why artists treated it as a private retreat. Picasso worked here in the summer of 1910. In the 1920s and '30s Dalí's family summer house became a hub: in the pivotal summer of 1929 Dalí hosted Luis Buñuel, René Magritte and Georgette, and the poet Paul Éluard with his wife Gala — who left with Dalí and never went back. Marcel Duchamp summered here for years and played chess on the front; Federico García Lorca, the writer Josep Pla, and later Mick Jagger and Gabriel García Márquez all passed through. Dalí called it 'el lugar más bonito del mundo.' A walking theme, not a ticket — trace it through the waterfront, L'Hostal, and the Museu de Cadaqués. · Free (self-guided walk). · Anytime. · Open in Google Maps →

culture:Cementiri de Cadaqués — graves a.name: Cementiri de Cadaqués — graves above the water
culture:Cementiri de Cadaqués — graves a.hook: A small hillside cemetery behind the church, its tombs looking straight out to the Mediterranean.
culture:Cementiri de Cadaqués — graves a.text: A small hillside cemetery behind the church, its tombs looking straight out to the Mediterranean. Reached by going around the back of Santa Maria, the village cemetery is a quiet terrace of whitewashed niches and family tombs stacked against the slope, every row facing the sea. It is modest — a handful of documented memorials — but the position, between the baroque church above and Dalí's bay below, makes it one of the calmer high points to take in the whole sweep of roofs, water and the Cucurucú rock. Free; walk up past Santa Maria and around the church. · Free. · Daytime open access. · Open in Google Maps →

culture:Es Poal — the cove Dalí painted.name: Es Poal — the cove Dalí painted at fifteen
culture:Es Poal — the cove Dalí painted.hook: The little shore where the young Dalí set his easel; subject of 'View of Cadaqués from Playa Poal,' 1920.
culture:Es Poal — the cove Dalí painted.text: The little shore where the young Dalí set his easel; subject of 'View of Cadaqués from Playa Poal,' 1920. Es Poal is one of the small calas fringing the bay, a working fishermen's shore of pulled-up boats that the teenage Dalí painted again and again — 'View of Cadaqués from Playa Poal' (1920) frames the white village across the calm water from here, with boats beached in the foreground. Standing on the pebbles, you can line the real bay up against the canvas: the same hump of houses, the same church on top. A short, free, deeply local stop on the waterfront walk. Free; part of the shoreline walk around the bay. · Free. · Anytime. · Open in Google Maps →

quartiers:Es Baluard / Old Town around S.name: Es Baluard / Old Town around Santa Maria
quartiers:Es Baluard / Old Town around S.text: The schist-paved upper warren climbing to the late-Gothic Església de Santa Maria (begun mid-16th c., on Carrer de Sant Isidre), whose Baroque gilt-wood altarpiece by Pau Costa frames the patroness, the Mare de Déu de l'Esperança. Streets average 3-4 m wide, paved in rastell — vertical slate slabs set on edge against the runoff.

quartiers:Sa Riba / Riba des Poal.name: Sa Riba / Riba des Poal
quartiers:Sa Riba / Riba des Poal.text: The seafront ribbon below the old town, running along the bay past Plaça des Portitxó. Here stands Casa Serinyana, the modernist Casa Blava built 1913-15 — one of the few non-whitewashed facades in the village.

quartiers:Es Poal.name: Es Poal
quartiers:Es Poal.text: The small cove and waterfront stretch of terraces and gelateries on the promenade, the aperitif-and-fish end of the bay where the boats pull up.

quartiers:Portlligat.name: Portlligat
quartiers:Portlligat.text: The sheltered cove 1.2 km north over the hill, a working anchorage of fishing huts that Dalí stitched together into his house from 1930; he lived and painted here until Gala's death in 1982, then moved to Púbol. Now the Casa Salvador Dalí house-museum.

quartiers:La Riera (Riera de Sant Vicenç.name: La Riera (Riera de Sant Vicenç)
quartiers:La Riera (Riera de Sant Vicenç.text: The dry torrent bed that splits the village and floods only in storms; its flat course hosts the Monday weekly market and serves as the main car artery and parking spine into town.

quartiers:Es Llané (Gran i Petit).name: Es Llané (Gran i Petit)
quartiers:Es Llané (Gran i Petit).text: Twin flat-rock urban beaches about five minutes south on foot — Llané Gran runs roughly 130 m long by 12 m wide. The Dalí family summered here before Portlligat.

quartiers:Sa Conca.name: Sa Conca
quartiers:Sa Conca.text: A stonier 90 m x 15 m beach about 1.2 km out toward the Cala Nans lighthouse, past the Llanés, with a long nudist tradition; also used as a free-concert space in the music festival.

quartiers:Es Portitxó / Es Portal.name: Es Portitxó / Es Portal
quartiers:Es Portitxó / Es Portal.text: The little square and old port-gate area where the village opens to the bay; the focal point for sardanes (e.g. on the Sant Sebastià aplec) and gatherings.

gastronomy:Celler Martín Faixó (Perafita.name: Celler Martín Faixó (Perafita / Cadac)
gastronomy:Celler Martín Faixó (Perafita.hook: Winery with vines ON Cap de Creus, by Cadaqués (slate, tramuntana)
gastronomy:Celler Martín Faixó (Perafita.text: Winery with vines ON Cap de Creus, by Cadaqués (slate, tramuntana) Family estate at Mas Sa Perafita, founded 2000 (first wines 2007), 11 ha on slate inside the natural park; labels Perafita and Cadac. Wine tourism since 2010: guided vineyard visits, tastings, pairings, vineyard hikes and rural-hotel stays. Booking by appointment via martinfaixo.com (phone listed on site as +34 972 258 954 — verify before relying on it). Road to Cadaqués, 17488 Cadaqués.

gastronomy:Mas Estela.name: Mas Estela
gastronomy:Mas Estela.hook: Biodynamic winery, La Selva de Mar (Alt Empordà)
gastronomy:Mas Estela.text: Biodynamic winery, La Selva de Mar (Alt Empordà) Soto-Dalmau family estate in the Sant Romà valley; ~50 ha bought 1989, organic from the start and biodynamic since 1999. Brands Vinya Selva de Mar, Quindals (some aged in clay amphorae), Moscatell Estela, Estela Dolç. Visits/tastings by arrangement via masestela.com; book ahead.

gastronomy:Espelt Viticultors.name: Espelt Viticultors
gastronomy:Espelt Viticultors.text: Large DO Empordà estate, Vilajuïga One of the biggest Empordà estates, with Garnatxa, Carinyena and Lledoner across the Alt Empordà. Listed by DO Empordà; visits by appointment (~2.5 h, around €27 with tasting per DO/visit listings — confirm current price), tours in Catalan, Spanish, English and French. Book via the winery.

gastronomy:Empordàlia (Oli de Pau + DO E.name: Empordàlia (Oli de Pau + DO Empordà wines)
gastronomy:Empordàlia (Oli de Pau + DO E.hook: Cooperative — wine and DOP olive oil, Pau & Vilajuïga
gastronomy:Empordàlia (Oli de Pau + DO E.text: Cooperative — wine and DOP olive oil, Pau & Vilajuïga Cooperative formed 2005 from the Pau (1961) and Vilajuïga (1947) co-ops. Makes DO Empordà wines and Oli de Pau extra-virgin oil from the local argudell and corivell olives off ~500 ha of old groves. Oil-mill and winery visits with tastings, plus a farm shop at Pau and Vilajuïga; book via empordalia.com.

gastronomy:Anxoves de l'Escala — Solés (.name: Anxoves de l'Escala — Solés (1888) & Callol i Serrats (1847)
gastronomy:Anxoves de l'Escala — Solés (.text: Anchovy salters, L'Escala (Alt Empordà) Two family salting houses curing 'Anxoves de l'Escala' in salt and hand-filleting them; Solés founded 1888, Fills de J. Callol i Serrats founded 1847. Callol i Serrats runs factory visits for groups and individuals; both have shops in L'Escala. Tour booking via the producers / Visit L'Escala tourism office.

bars:Garnatxa de l'Empordà (vi dolç).name: Garnatxa de l'Empordà (vi dolç)
bars:Garnatxa de l'Empordà (vi dolç).hook: The DO's fortified jewel — sun-dried Garnatxa stopped with spirit, 14–20% alcohol.
bars:Garnatxa de l'Empordà (vi dolç).text: The DO's fortified jewel — sun-dried Garnatxa stopped with spirit, 14–20% alcohol. €€–€€€ (500ml) A traditional fortified sweet wine of DO Empordà (DO recognised 1975; renamed DO Empordà 2006). Min. 90% Garnatxa (lledoner blanc, grey, or red lledoner roig), grapes over-ripened and sun-dried after harvest (straw-wine method), fermentation halted with grape spirit to retain natural sugar; jammy, spiced, oxidative. Drink with desserts or aged cheese. Producers: Espolla (Celler Cooperatiu d'Espolla) · Mas Estela (Estela Dolç) · Empordàlia

bars:Garnatxa Negra (Empordà red).name: Garnatxa Negra (Empordà red)
bars:Garnatxa Negra (Empordà red).hook: Black Grenache off slate and tramuntana — the workhorse red of Cap de Creus country.
bars:Garnatxa Negra (Empordà red).text: Black Grenache off slate and tramuntana — the workhorse red of Cap de Creus country. €€ Garnatxa Negra (lledoner negre) is the leading black variety of DO Empordà (recognised 1975), grown on llicorella/slate soils on the Pyrenean and Cap de Creus flanks; warm, ripe-fruited, often blended with Carinyena. Martín Faixó grows it on Cap de Creus slate near Cadaqués. Producers: Martín Faixó (Perafita / Cadac labels, Cadaqués) · Espelt Viticultors (Vilajuïga) · Vinyes dels Aspres (Cantallops)

bars:Carinyena / Samsó (Empordà).name: Carinyena / Samsó (Empordà)
bars:Carinyena / Samsó (Empordà).hook: The drought-hardy old-vine red the Empordà builds its structure on.
bars:Carinyena / Samsó (Empordà).text: The drought-hardy old-vine red the Empordà builds its structure on. €€ Carinyena (Samsó) is the Empordà's other principal variety, prized for old, low-yielding bush vines; resists drought and gives high total acidity and structure. Often co-planted/blended with Garnatxa. Cap de Creus monks grew vines here from the Middle Ages; phylloxera hit in 1879. Producers: Espelt Viticultors · Vinyes dels Aspres · Empordàlia

bars:Lledoner / Garnatxa Blanca & Roig (.name: Lledoner / Garnatxa Blanca & Roig (white & grey)
bars:Lledoner / Garnatxa Blanca & Roig (.hook: The pale Garnatxas — white lledoner and the rare red-berried lledoner roig.
bars:Lledoner / Garnatxa Blanca & Roig (.text: The pale Garnatxas — white lledoner and the rare red-berried lledoner roig. €€ DO Empordà grows the full Garnatxa family: white (lledoner blanc), grey, and the red-berried lledoner roig recognised by its coloured skins. Used in fresh dry whites/rosats and in the sweet vi dolç. Espelt bottles a Lledoner rosat listed by DO Empordà. Producers: Espelt Viticultors (Lledoner rosat) · Martín Faixó (Perafita whites, Cadaqués) · Empordàlia

bars:Cap de Creus slate wine — Martín Fa.name: Cap de Creus slate wine — Martín Faixó (Perafita / Cadac)
bars:Cap de Creus slate wine — Martín Fa.hook: The one winery with vines actually on the Cap de Creus peninsula by Cadaqués.
bars:Cap de Creus slate wine — Martín Fa.text: The one winery with vines actually on the Cap de Creus peninsula by Cadaqués. €€–€€€ Family estate (Rafa & Carme Martín; daughter Ester winemaker), founded 2000, first wines 2007. 11 ha of vines on slate between Cadaqués, Roses and Port de la Selva, inside Cap de Creus Natural Park; varieties incl. Garnatxa, Cabernet, Merlot, Picapoll, Muscat of Alexandria. Labels Perafita and Cadac. An underground winery, fought over for ~20 years of permits, was set to begin in 2026. NOTE: bottle output is reported as 50,000 (estate site) and 70,000 (ARA interview) — figure unverified. Producers: Celler Martín Faixó (Mas Sa Perafita, Cadaqués)

bars:Ratafia (IGP Ratafia Catalana).name: Ratafia (IGP Ratafia Catalana)
bars:Ratafia (IGP Ratafia Catalana).hook: Green-walnut and herb digestif from the farmhouse mortar — drunk after the meal.
bars:Ratafia (IGP Ratafia Catalana).text: Green-walnut and herb digestif from the farmhouse mortar — drunk after the meal. €€ (700ml) Catalan herbal liqueur protected as IGP Ratafia Catalana: unripe green walnuts (picked before the shell hardens) macerated with rosemary, thyme, sage, oregano and many other herbs/flowers for a minimum of 40 days, then often aged ~3 months in wood. Sweet, tannic, dark; served as a digestif, classically with carquinyolis. Producers: Numerous Empordà/Girona family and small producers (e.g. Ratafia de l'Ermità)

bars:Cremat (rom cremat).name: Cremat (rom cremat)
bars:Cremat (rom cremat).hook: Flamed Caribbean rum, coffee and cinnamon — the havaneres night in a clay pot.
bars:Cremat (rom cremat).text: Flamed Caribbean rum, coffee and cinnamon — the havaneres night in a clay pot. € (a glass, festival/bar) Dark rum heated with sugar, cinnamon, lemon peel and roasted coffee beans, then flamed and stirred until ~a third of the alcohol burns off (~10 min), doused with brewed coffee, served hot. Roots in 19th-c. Catalan–Cuba trade; bound to the havaneres sea-shanty tradition. Heartland is Calella de Palafrugell (Cantada d'Havaneres since 1966, Port-Bo trio); reaches Cadaqués and the coast in summer. Producers: Not bottled — made tableside at havaneres nights and Costa Brava taverns

music:Festival Internacional de Música d.name: Festival Internacional de Música de Cadaqués
music:Festival Internacional de Música d.hook: Catalonia's second-oldest summer festival, born in the church in August 1970.
music:Festival Internacional de Música d.text: Catalonia's second-oldest summer festival, born in the church in August 1970. Founded in 1970 — the second-oldest festival on the Costa Brava after Sant Feliu's Porta Ferrada — it runs across roughly April to December (10 concerts in the 52nd edition, 2025) split between the Església de Santa Maria and the Espai Art i Joia. The 2025 line-up ranged from the Orquestra Barroca Catalana and guitarist Carles Trepat to a trumpet-and-saxophone night with Mireia Farrés and Llibert Fortuny, closing 27 December with mezzo-soprano Titon Frauca and organist Pau Riuró. In 1988 the festival spun off its own Orquestra de Cadaqués.

music:Church concerts in Santa Maria.name: Church concerts in Santa Maria
music:Church concerts in Santa Maria.hook: Baroque and chamber programmes under the 23-metre gilded altarpiece.
music:Church concerts in Santa Maria.text: Baroque and chamber programmes under the 23-metre gilded altarpiece. The festival uses the nave of Santa Maria for its acoustics: 2025 dates included the Cor i Orquestra de l'Orfeó Gracienc (13 April), the Orquestra Barroca Catalana (24 May), Carles Trepat solo guitar (5 July) and the Quartet Prysma (23 August), most at 19:00. Hearing a Bach partita or a baroque ensemble beneath the Pau Costa retaule is the single most site-specific musical experience in the village.

music:Havaneres & cremat.name: Havaneres & cremat
music:Havaneres & cremat.hook: Cuban-rooted sea-shanties sung over flamed rum-coffee.
music:Havaneres & cremat.text: Cuban-rooted sea-shanties sung over flamed rum-coffee. The Costa Brava's signature ritual: havaneres — choral songs in the rhythm of the Cuban contradansa, carried back by 19th-century Catalan sailors trading with Cuba — sung while cremat (rum, sugar, cinnamon, lemon peel and coffee, flambéed in a cauldron) burns blue in the dark. The genre's epicentre is the Cantada d'Havaneres at nearby Calella de Palafrugell on the first Saturday of July, where choirs like Port Bo perform; Cadaqués and the other Empordà ports keep the tradition in summer terrace sing-alongs.

music:Cap Roig Festival (nearby).name: Cap Roig Festival (nearby)
music:Cap Roig Festival (nearby).hook: Big-name open-air pop in a clifftop botanical garden, ~79 km down the coast.
music:Cap Roig Festival (nearby).text: Big-name open-air pop in a clifftop botanical garden, ~79 km down the coast. Held in the gardens of Cap Roig at Calella de Palafrugell (about 79 km / just over an hour by road from Cadaqués), the festival ran 12 July–18 August in 2025 with headliners including Tom Jones, James Blunt, Franz Ferdinand, Simple Minds and Sopa de Cabra. It is the region's heavyweight summer concert series — the place to go for arena acts when Cadaqués itself stays small and acoustic.

music:The village's musical clan — the P.name: The village's musical clan — the Pitxots
music:The village's musical clan — the P.hook: The family of musicians and painters who first pulled Dalí into Cadaqués culture.
music:The village's musical clan — the P.text: The family of musicians and painters who first pulled Dalí into Cadaqués culture. Cadaqués's deepest musical thread is local: the Pitxot (Pichot) family — among them the painter Ramon Pitxot, who first showed the young Dalí modern painting, and the operatic and instrumental musicians of the same clan — were the artistic dynasty that made the village a salon long before the festival. Their legacy surfaces in the rotating shows at the Museu de Cadaqués, which has mounted Dalí-and-Pitxot exhibitions tying the family's music and art to the bay.

avoid:Driving out to the Cap de Creus li.name: Driving out to the Cap de Creus lighthouse in high summer
avoid:Driving out to the Cap de Creus li.text: The access road beyond the village is closed to private cars on restricted days roughly June-August; you'll be turned back or stuck. Instead: Park free at Corral d'en Morell in town and take the shuttle to the lighthouse, or hike/cycle the coastal track — and check the day's rules with the Parc Natural or Ajuntament first.

avoid:Coming in August expecting an easy.name: Coming in August expecting an easy day-trip
avoid:Coming in August expecting an easy.text: The single GI-614 backs up for kilometres and in-town parking in July-August is brutal; the village's narrow schist lanes can't absorb the load. Instead: Visit in the May-June or Sept-Oct shoulder, or if you must come in August, arrive at dawn and walk in from the outer lots rather than circling.

avoid:Booking a boat or cape excursion w.name: Booking a boat or cape excursion without checking the tramuntana
avoid:Booking a boat or cape excursion w.text: This is one of the windiest stretches of the Catalan coast; gusts over 100 km/h can cancel small-craft movement and make Cap de Creus brutally exposed. Instead: Read the Meteocat / Ports de la Generalitat marine forecast the night before and keep a wind-free fallback (old town, Casa Dalí, a long lunch).

avoid:Turning up at Casa Salvador Dalí w.name: Turning up at Casa Salvador Dalí without a timed reservation
avoid:Turning up at Casa Salvador Dalí w.text: Entry is by pre-booked timed slot only and groups enter at fixed intervals; walk-ups are routinely turned away, and the house closes entirely 7 Jan-11 Feb. Instead: Book a dated, timed ticket in advance on salvador-dali.org and arrive ~30 minutes early to collect it.

follow:Meteocat / Ports de la Generalita.name: Meteocat / Ports de la Generalitat — tramuntana & marine forecast
follow:Meteocat / Ports de la Generalita.text: The Cadaqués / Cap de Creus wind and sea forecast — check the night before any boat day for >100 km/h gusts.

follow:Fundació Gala-Salvador Dalí (salv.text: Timed-entry booking, hours and winter closure (7 Jan-11 Feb) for the Casa Salvador Dalí house-museum at Portlligat.

follow:Festival Internacional de Música.text: The April-December concert programme, venues (Santa Maria, Sala de l'Amistat, Sa Conca) and tickets.
